data.generation: Target data distribution p0 is a 1D symmetric Gaussian mixture 0.5 N(-2, 0.3^2) + 0.5 N(2, 0.3^2), sampled directly (no trajectories). Forward VP-SDE samples x_t = alpha(t) x0 + sqrt(1 - alpha(t)^2) z are drawn analytically from the perturbation kernel; t is sampled uniform on [0.02, 1] for distillation queries. Splits are disjoint by data sample x0 (never by (t, z) draw within a sample).

distillation.library_variables: Polynomials in (x, tau), where tau = 1 - t is reverse time (tau in [0, 1]). The teacher reverse drift is f_rev(x, tau) = 0.5 beta(s) x + beta(s) s_theta(x, s) with s = 1 - tau; the teacher diffusion is g_rev(tau) = sqrt(beta(s)), a function of tau only (the paper's diffusion schedule is known, not learned).
distillation.oracle_diagnostic: the same SINDy procedure fitted to ground-truth reverse-field values at the same query states (diagnostic ceiling only, not a candidate)
distillation.query_states: forward-kernel samples (x_t, tau = 1 - t) from split-disjoint data samples; teacher evaluated directly (no finite differences)
distillation.selection: per field, minimize validation NRMSE against the teacher; test evaluated once after selection

ground_truth_sde.beta: beta(t) = 0.1 + 19.9 t, t in [0, 1] (the paper's VP-SDE schedule)
ground_truth_sde.forward: dx = -0.5 beta(t) x dt + sqrt(beta(t)) dW (VP-SDE); perturbation kernel N(alpha(t) x0, 1 - alpha(t)^2) with alpha(t) = exp(-0.5 (0.1 t + 9.95 t^2))
ground_truth_sde.reverse_drift: f_rev(x, tau) = 0.5 beta(s) x + beta(s) score_true(x, s), s = 1 - tau, where score_true is the analytic score of the perturbed mixture (means +-2 alpha(s), variance 1 - 0.91 alpha(s)^2)

H2_diffusion_distillation.note: Headline is the g NRMSE; the Sigma clause is the identified-object clause (Sigma = g^2 in 1D). H2c is the structure clause: the paper's diffusion is tau-only, so a faithful symbolic g must be nearly x-independent; it is judged by the across-x relative spread at fixed tau, not by coefficient inspection.

x_independence.definition: max over tau in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75} of std_x(symbolic g(x, tau)) / mean_x(symbolic g(x, tau)) over x in [-4, 4]

H3_truth_recovery.note: Field-level clauses only. No coefficient clause: the truth reverse drift is a rational mixture-score function, not a polynomial, so coefficient comparison against truth is meaningless (Day 1 lesson adapted). The collinearity gate is still computed at the maximum selectable degree and reported; if it exceeds 10, any coefficient-level reading of the selected polynomial is reported as indeterminate.

H4_simulation.domain_excursion_definition: fraction of simulated samples whose |X| ever exceeds 8.0 at any simulated step; a domain-validity measure separate from failure (Day 4 reflection)
H4_simulation.mode_mass_definition: fraction of final samples with |X| > 1 (the truth mixture has essentially all mass in [-3, -1] U [1, 3]); reported for teacher, symbolic, no-score baseline and truth samples
H4_simulation.note: Reverse sampling from the prior N(0, 1) at tau = 0 to tau = 1 with paired Brownian increments; failure is non-finite state or |X| > 30. Paired RMSE is secondary (reverse paths diverge stochastically even for identical fields); the distribution clauses (W1 and mode mass) carry the verdict.

H5_paper_axis_reverse_vs_noscore_and_pfo.no_score_baseline: reverse drift with the score term dropped: f = 0.5 beta(s) x only (plain OU reversal); same diffusion and same prior draws and increments
H5_paper_axis_reverse_vs_noscore_and_pfo.note: MAIN clauses are absolute levels (Day 7 reflection): teacher and symbolic W1 and mode mass against truth samples, plus the no-score baseline's separation judged by absolute W1 and mode-mass levels. The probability-flow ODE with the teacher score (deterministic, drift 0.5 beta x + 0.5 beta score) is reported as a diagnostic only, with no frozen clause, because the paper's ODE/SDE equivalence is a marginal statement, not a paired-path statement.

H6_discretization_bias_reverse_step.coarsening: teacher reverse SDE simulated with dt = 0.05 (20 steps) vs dt = 0.002 (500 steps); coarse increments are exact sums of the fine increments over each 25-step block (common random numbers, properly paired); same prior draws
H6_discretization_bias_reverse_step.note: Day 1 reflection adapted to reverse-time SDEs: the estimator here is denoising score matching, not EM, so the discretization axis is the reverse solver step, not the teacher-training step. Regime split (Day 1 linear/nonlinear analogue): teacher drift error vs truth on test queries in the near-linear regime (tau < 0.3, s > 0.7, prior-like, score near -x) vs the nonlinear regime (tau > 0.7, s < 0.3, sharp bimodal score). Per-step SNR (|f_truth| dt / (g sqrt(dt)) at dt = 0.01) is quantified by regime (Day 7 lesson).
H6_discretization_bias_reverse_step.regime_gap_note: nonlinear-regime teacher drift NRMSE vs truth minus near-linear-regime NRMSE >= 0.05
H6_discretization_bias_reverse_step.w1_degradation_note: W1(coarse samples vs truth) - W1(fine samples vs truth) >= 0.03

H7_downstream_one_step.note: One-step reverse predictions from test query states: predicted mean x + f_rev(x, tau) dt vs the realized next state under the TRUTH reverse SDE with dt = 0.01 and fixed increments. |MSE_symbolic - MSE_teacher| with paired SE; if paired SE >= 0.001 (half the threshold) the clause is reported as 'not statistically established' even if the point estimate passes (Day 4 reflection).

paper.authors: Yang Song, Jascha Sohl-Dickstein, Diederik P. Kingma, Abhishek Kumar, Stefano Ermon, Ben Poole
paper.experiment: Sections 3-4: forward SDE dx = f(x, t) dt + g(t) dW transforming data to a prior, reverse-time SDE dx = [f(x, t) - g(t)^2 nabla log p_t(x)] dt + g(t) dWbar driven by a learned time-dependent score network trained by denoising score matching; VP-SDE (and VE-SDE) instantiations, a predictor-corrector sampler, and an equivalent probability-flow ODE enabling exact likelihoods. Benchmarks on CIFAR-10 and high-resolution images.
paper.title: Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations

reflections_applied.day1_collinearity_gate_at_max_degree: VIF is computed on train queries for the degree-3 full (x, tau) library (the maximum degree the selection procedure can choose), with the constant column excluded (Day 8 lesson). No coefficient hypothesis is frozen against truth because the truth reverse drift is not polynomial; the gate's role is to block coefficient-level readings of the selected polynomial if exceeded.
reflections_applied.day1_discretization_bias: H6 is the adapted discretization-bias diagnostic: reverse-solver step 0.002 vs 0.05 with exactly aggregated common-random-number increments, regime-split (near-linear tau < 0.3 vs nonlinear tau > 0.7) with per-step SNR quantified by regime, and drift error interpreted separately from sampling W1.
reflections_applied.day2_off_manifold: Off-manifold diagnostic is standard: a fixed (x, tau) grid, x in [-4, 4], tau in {0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95}, for f_rev and g_rev, reported on field / off-manifold axes separately and used for reporting only, never for selection (Day 5). Three-way comparison (symbolic vs teacher, teacher vs truth, symbolic vs truth) per Day 9.
reflections_applied.day4_domain_validity: H4 carries a domain clause separate from failure (excursion |X| > 8).
reflections_applied.day4_downstream_paired_se: H7 reports a paired SE with a pre-frozen indeterminate rule.
reflections_applied.day5_distribution_vs_field: Distribution metrics (W1, mode mass) and field metrics (drift/g NRMSE) are reported side by side and never substituted for each other; the teacher's DSM loss is reported alongside its field error so a small training loss is not read as field recovery. Many prior draws (no single initial condition).
reflections_applied.day5_off_manifold_denominator: Grid NRMSE values above 1 are reported with absolute RMS errors alongside.
reflections_applied.day6_diffusion_input_design: Diffusion is fitted and verified separately from drift (its own full (x, tau) library and verdict, plus the tau-only structure clause H2c).
reflections_applied.day7_absolute_levels_for_shift: H5's main clauses are absolute W1 and mode-mass levels for teacher, symbolic and the no-score baseline, not only a degradation/difference.
reflections_applied.day9_grid_three_way: The (x, tau) grid reports symbolic vs teacher, teacher vs truth, and symbolic vs truth together, so grid mismatch is attributed to the teacher's off-manifold wildness vs the symbolic approximation separately.

split.unit: data sample x0 (disjoint; (t, z) draws within a sample are never split across splits)

teacher.architecture: Epsilon-network: MLP [64, 64] tanh on inputs (x / 2.5, t); output epsilon_theta(x, t); score s_theta(x, t) = -epsilon_theta(x, t) / sqrt(1 - alpha(t)^2). Trained by denoising score matching: fresh (x0, t, z) draws per step, loss ||epsilon_theta(x_t, t) - z||^2, Adam lr 1e-3, 4000 steps, batch 512. Teacher reverse drift = 0.5 beta(s) x + beta(s) s_theta(x, s); teacher diffusion = sqrt(beta(s)) (the paper's known schedule).
teacher.deviation_from_paper: Three declared cuts. (1) Images (CIFAR-10, 1024x1024) are replaced by a 1D bimodal Gaussian mixture whose perturbed scores are analytic, so teacher-vs-truth field comparison is exact; results say nothing about the paper's image benchmarks. (2) The score network is a small MLP on (x, t), not the paper's U-Net/RefineNet image architecture, and the predictor-corrector sampler is not used (plain Euler-Maruyama reverse sampling, so discretization effects are visible rather than corrected away). (3) Only the VP-SDE is treated (VE-SDE, sub-VP-SDE and conditional generation are out of scope); the probability-flow ODE is a diagnostic, not a fitted model.
teacher.estimator: denoising score matching (DSM) on the VP-SDE perturbation kernel
